chunks: Abd al-Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdus al-Naysaburi al-Attar told us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaybah told us, saying: Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi narrated from Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them), saying:
The actions of the servants are created. I said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, what is the meaning of 'created'? He said: Predestined.
ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Rida mean when he says human actions are 'created'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the theological nuance of 'created actions' by equating 'mukhalaqa' with 'mugaddara' (predestined/determined), thereby affirming the Shia doctrine of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (the matter between the two matters). This explanation reconciles divine omnipotence with human agency, asserting that while God creates the power and capacity for action, humans acquire (*kasb*) the specific deeds through their free will, avoiding the extremes of absolute determinism (*jabr*) and total independence (*tafrid*).
